$comment: Tony's Pizza Fantasy — locked palette. 32 shared colours, plus a narrowly typed per-family extension. Every generated asset is quantized to these values during processing; this file is the mechanism that keeps independently generated batches looking like one world. Do not add, remove, or edit a color without regenerating every affected asset.
status: PROVISIONAL — locked on approval of art test batch B0

ink.role: Outlines, text, shadow anchors. Warm-biased so it never reads as pure black.

wood.role: Paneling, tables, counter, booth frames, floors.

red.role: Checkered cloth, vinyl booths, sauce, signage.

paper.role: Menus, newspaper, receipts, napkins, pizza-box print.

amber.role: Incandescent light, warm key, cheese, brass, lamp glow.

blue.role: Night, cool ambient fill, Detroit-adjacent jerseys, cold neon.

violet.role: Deep shadow in the underground, epic treatment, neon accent.

skin.role: Avatar and character skin. Four steps spanning a usable range. Managers select a step; it is not tied to any other palette role.

familyExtensions.$comment: Colours available to ONE asset family only. The shared 32 stay shared. A family extension is how a measured coverage gap gets closed without rewriting art that does not have the gap, and its SIZE is a measured property of that family's art rather than a convention -- see docs/PALETTE_FIDELITY_BOUNDARY.md. Derive with `npx tsx scripts/derive-family-palette.mts <family> <count>`; the hexes are literals here and are never recomputed at build time.

zone.$comment: The room's own 64. `zone_*` assets are large painterly interiors: the shell arrives as a 941x1672 painting with 153,738 distinct colours and 2.9% blockiness -- a continuous-tone illustration, not pixel art. Against the shared 32 it quantized to a mean error of 35 of a possible 441, with the paper ramp taking 0.1% of the pixels and the amber (lamp-glow) ramp 27.3%, which is why the room read as lit by sodium light. Four colours (the 2026-08-05 pass) took that to 21.6 and were still visibly orange and posterized at phone resolution. Sixty-four take it to 5.4 and are visually indistinguishable from the approved source. Ordered by the share of the family each carries.

character.$comment: Tony's own 16. He arrives 480x1315 with 72,004 colours. The shared 32 have no yellow-orange for his skin, so it landed on the skin ramp's muddy tans and his face lost the source's warmth entirely; his jersey blue and apron cream were served no better. Sixteen colours take his mean error from 30.3 to 14.5 while keeping his shading contiguous -- more than that raises the isolated-pixel rate without improving what the face looks like, which is measured in docs/PALETTE_FIDELITY_BOUNDARY.md.

semantic.$comment: Semantic roles map to ramp entries. Never introduce a new hex for a semantic role.
semantic.shadowRule: one step darker within the same ramp — never ink-900, never pure black

rarity.$comment: Rarity must never be communicated by color alone. These reinforce the frame geometry and label required by 06 §8.

prohibited.$comment: Never sample or introduce these, regardless of what a generation returns.
prohibited.note: Pure black flattens the warm bias; pure white blows out against paper-white. Both are common image-model defaults and must be quantized away.
